title: Ten obstacles
hook: a desk buried in mail and chargers; Buddhaghosa lists ten things that snag a meditating mind, books included
tomorrow: why would a pond make a bad place to meditate?

segments.voice: Yesterday: a friend chooses, and you still do the walking. Before the walking starts, Buddhaghosa checks the path for rocks.

A desk buried in mail, two chargers, and a mug from Tuesday. You sit down to do one thing, and your hand keeps shuffling the clutter instead. Buddhaghosa has a list for exactly that, and it answers yesterday's question. A house. Family. Gain. Students. Building work. Travel. Relatives. Illness. Study. And powers. Ten things that can get in the way of meditation. Yes, books made the list.
screen: `MAIL, CHARGERS, A TUESDAY MUG.` → `A HOUSE, FAMILY, EVEN BOOKS.` → `TEN THINGS IN THE WAY.`

segments.voice: The word is palibodha: an obstacle, a snag, something that holds you back. Look at the list again, and notice that most of it is good. A home. Family. Gifts. Students. A building project. A trip. Your relatives. Study. None of these is bad. As Buddhaghosa describes them, they become obstacles when the mind keeps going back to them: the unfinished roof, the visit you owe, the book half-read. His advice is practical, almost like a to-do list. Finish the building work, or hand it over. Put off the trip. Treat the illness with medicine. Set the books aside for a while. And the strangest item, powers, the unusual abilities said to come with deep meditation: he says they get in the way of insight, not of concentration. Even something impressive can be a snag. Here's the part to feel rather than think. An obstacle has a texture. It's a tug on your attention, like a sleeve caught on a nail, and the body often notices it before the mind can name it. Clearing the way doesn't mean giving up your family or your home. It means finding which thing is tugging, and loosening that one.
screen: `PALIBODHA: A SNAG.` · `MOSTLY GOOD THINGS THAT TUG.` · `FINISH IT, POSTPONE IT, SET IT DOWN.` · `A SLEEVE CAUGHT ON A NAIL.` · then, large: `CLEAR THE WAY.`

segments.voice: Find one small thing within reach that has been tugging at you: a cup, a pile of mail, a phone face up. Clear it: put it away, turn it over, set it outside the room. Then rest your palm on the cleared spot and feel the empty space under your hand for the rest of the sit.
Palibodha: an obstacle, a snag. Buddhaghosa lists ten that can get in the way of meditation, from a house to powers.
Keep this: clear the way, one snag at a time, starting with the one that tugs. Four of forty.

howItsDone: Before a retreat, Buddhist meditators may settle their affairs, finish or hand over work, and put travel on hold, so that the mind isn't pulled back to them during practice.

fork.setup: your sister's wedding is in two weeks, and you've promised yourself a daily sit. the wedding prep keeps tugging. what fits Buddhaghosa's advice?
options: keep the sit short for now and go deeper after the wedding.
skip the wedding prep, because meditation comes before family.
wait until life has no obstacles at all, then begin.
fork.reveal: Buddhaghosa's obstacles are handled, not fled: finish the work, postpone the trip, treat the illness. family stays; the snag gets loosened.

chat.meaning: Buddhaghosa's obstacles are mostly good things that snag the mind. You don't give them up; you finish, postpone or set aside the one tugging.

palibodha.meaning: Pali: an obstacle or snag that holds the mind back

Buddhaghosa.meaning: the Theravada scholar-monk who wrote the Visuddhimagga

insight.meaning: vipassana: seeing things clearly as they are

concentration.meaning: samadhi: the mind steady and gathered on one object
